messages:
Zoe Park: Dropping a compact iteration for the latency card. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EX/latency-compact-v2

Proposal:
- p95 shown as a left-aligned headline with small unit (ms).
- Heatmap full width beneath.
- Timepicker on top-right; sampling moved inline to left of presets as a tiny select labeled 'Sampling'.
- When sampling != Off show a subtle pill: 'Sampled • 10%'; pill opens a persistent help region for screen readers.
- On narrow widths collapse the sparkline and tuck the pill into overflow.

Quick feedback please on wording and keyboard flow.

Liam O'Connor: Nice — compact and scannable. A couple asks:
- Pill should expose plain text in DOM like "Sampled 10%" so it can be copied/announced.
- Select hit target >=44px.
- Tooltip copy: "Sampled: view shows a subset of requests; numbers are approximate." Keep it one sentence.

Nina Patel: Accessibility notes:
- Use button+listbox pattern for the sampling control and put the current selection as visible text node.
- Pill must have aria-describedby pointing to the help region node (no hover-only tooltips).
- Keyboard: Tab order should be presets -> sampling -> calendar -> Apply. Ensure Left/Right change selection when listbox open.

Omar Khalid: Product/infra:
- Please record sampling_percent in the query metadata so we can reproduce views.
- If sampling <5% show a low-confidence indicator on the pill (orange dot + title 'Low confidence').
- If the p95 value is computed from sampled data prefix with an asterisk and link to docs.

a11y-bot: Checklist added to INFR-4722:
- [ ] Sampling control uses accessible button+listbox pattern
- [ ] Pill exposes visible DOM text and aria-describedby
- [ ] Hit target >=44px
- [ ] Sampling_percent wired to query metadata
- [ ] Low-confidence state when percent <5%
Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-4722

Zoe Park: Thanks all 604 I'll update Figma with pill DOM text and add the low-confidence treatment. Scheduling a 15m playtest Thu 9:30am PT for keyboard flow + responsive collapse. Invite: @Nina Patel @Liam O'Connor @Omar Khalid.
